title: The localizing closure exists
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring (not necessarily commutative) [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], $X$ a scheme with its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ its pulled-back ring object [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ for its category of left module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\mathcal A)$ for its unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All small sums and site skeletons use the fixed universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal S$ be any class of objects of this derived category (for instance, when $\Lambda$ is commutative, $\mathcal S=\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]).

1. $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has arbitrary small direct sums, computed termwise on complexes, and the direct sum of distinguished triangles is distinguished [def-weil-triangulated-category].
2. The intersection of all full triangulated subcategories of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ that contain $\mathcal S$, are closed under isomorphisms, and are closed under arbitrary small direct sums, is again such a subcategory. It is denoted $\Loc(\mathcal S)$; it is the smallest localizing subcategory containing $\mathcal S$. Here localizing means full, triangulated, closed under isomorphisms and under these sums.
3. $\Loc(\mathcal S)$ is closed under direct summands, hence thick [pur9-def-thick]; and $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal S'\subseteq\Loc(\mathcal S)$ implies $\Loc(\mathcal S')=\Loc(\mathcal S)$.

external.place: By exactness of direct sums, the acyclic complexes form a localizing subcategory of $K(\Lambda_X)$; for a Verdier quotient by a subcategory closed under coproducts, the quotient functor preserves coproducts (Neeman, *Triangulated categories*, Lemma 3.2.10).

proof.text: Apply the existing source theorem CategoryTheory.Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian directly to internal left modules over the pulled-back ring object. Its actual Lean statement requires only MonObj, not IsCommMonObj. The ambient abelian sheaves are Grothendieck and their closed tensor preserves colimits, so no sectionwise ring reconstruction is needed.

Install the existing Grothendieck K-injective resolution instance. The theorem derived_hasCoproducts supplies all coproducts indexed in Type (u+1). Use HomologicalComplex.coconeOfHasColimitEval for a family of complexes: its evaluation in each degree is the chosen coproduct, and isColimit_mapCocone_grothendieckSum proves that its specified coprojections become a coproduct after Q. This includes empty families.

source.place: Tags 079Q and 07D9; existing K-injective and termwise coproduct theorems

proof.text: Transport each triangle T_i through triangleOpEquivalence to the opposite category. Mathlib productTriangle_distinguished says their product U is distinguished. Its inverse image Z in the original category is distinguished by unop_distinguished. The morphisms T_i to Z are obtained from the product projections, followed contravariantly by the inverse functor and the inverse unit. The unit has identity vertex components. Therefore the three vertex cofans have injections given by the unop product projections. Their universal properties follow explicitly by taking opposites of product lifts, with factorization and uniqueness from productIsProduct. This constructs the required cofan including its connecting maps, and works for the empty family.

source.place: productTriangle_distinguished, with Opposite/Pretriangulated.lean: triangleOpEquivalence and unop_distinguished

proof.text: For the landed intersection localizingClosure S, prove repleteness, zero containment, shift stability and extension closure by testing any localizing predicate P containing S. Its corresponding closure condition applies pointwise. The same argument uses P's existing-coproduct condition for all ambient object-universe families. Thus the intersection is localizing. Every element of S satisfies every such P, proving containment; evaluating the defining universal quantifier at a candidate P proves minimality.

Let P=Loc(S). First turn P's existing ambient-object-universe coproduct closure into IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape. For I in Type (u+1), reindex along Discrete(ULift.{u+2} I) equivalent to Discrete I. Since the ambient derived category has I-indexed coproducts, P.FullSubcategory has them too. The proved countable-coproduct theorem makes it idempotent complete. For a retract K of L in P, regard r.r followed by r.i as an idempotent of the full-subcategory object L. Split it there as K'. The maps r.i followed by the splitting projection and the splitting inclusion followed by r.r exhibit K isomorphic to K'. Their inverse equations follow from the retract equation and the two splitting equations. Since P is replete, K lies in P. This is direct-summand closure, hence thickness.

source.place: Tag 05QW (countable coproducts imply idempotent completeness); uniqueness of idempotent splittings

proof.text: If S is contained in S' and S' in Loc(S), apply the intersection formula for Loc(S') to the candidate Loc(S), obtaining Loc(S') ≤ Loc(S). Conversely every localizing P containing S' contains S, so any member of Loc(S) lies in P. This gives the reverse inclusion, and antisymmetry proves equality.

proof_origin.place: (1)-(3), implemented by P1 using the existing internal-module Grothendieck theorem, duality from Mathlib triangle products, pointwise intersection, and the proved countable-coproduct idempotent-completeness theorem

lean.statement: theorem localizingClosure_exists (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj Λ] (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))] (S : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)))) : HasCoproducts.{u + 1} (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))) ∧ (∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) (K : I → CochainComplex (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)) ℤ), ∃ c : Cofan K, (∀ n : ℤ, Nonempty (IsColimit ((HomologicalComplex.eval _ _ n).mapCocone c))) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (DerivedCategory.Q.mapCocone c))) ∧ (∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) (T : I → Triangle (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)))), (∀ i : I, T i ∈ distTriang _) → ∃ c : Cofan T, Nonempty (IsColimit (Triangle.π₁.mapCocone c)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Triangle.π₂.mapCocone c)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Triangle.π₃.mapCocone c)) ∧ c.pt ∈ distTriang _) ∧ IsLocalizingSubcategory (localizingClosure S) ∧ (S ≤ localizingClosure S) ∧ (∀ P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))), IsLocalizingSubcategory P → S ≤ P → localizingClosure S ≤ P) ∧ (localizingClosure S).IsStableUnderRetracts ∧ (∀ S' : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))), S ≤ S' → S' ≤ localizingClosure S → localizingClosure S' = localizingClosure S)
